intent_snapshot.goal: On Claude Code, a literal-user imm-run entry mints a session- and workspace-bound entry token. Enrollment and unattended batch start keep one native gate per entry, because a same-uid model write can forge the token; under a live token stale batch retirement and same-Host recovery open no gate. A confirmed batch start prints a non-blocking execution manifest, and the token is invalidated by session exit, workspace change or a Stop-boundary pause (Spec D1-D4, D6, D11; ADR 0025).

acceptance.assertion: After a UserPromptSubmit carrying a literal imm-run entry, enroll and start_unattended_batch each open exactly one native gate, and a declined gate claims nothing even with a live token; a later retire_stale_batch under that token completes with no elicitation/create request and records a confirmation_ref of kind entry_token still bound to the plan digest; a rework-exit confirmation still opens elicitation with its exits.

Each of these is refused with no Kernel mutation: an authority tool call with no prior literal entry; a call whose session id differs from the minting session; a call after SessionEnd; a call from a different workspace realpath; a call after the run paused at the Stop boundary; a tool argument that supplies a token or native_decision field.

A confirmed start_unattended_batch result carries a manifest listing every child's task id, risk, scope summary and verification commands; a lane-mode batch dialog under a live token still offers the Lane revision delegation choice; and the token stays live across a same-session continuation until the bound run is terminal.

attestations.summary: Provenance verified (5affcab, only parent ab8999f, tree 95c97c8). The round-3 delta is test-only. It adds an end-to-end retire seam test (literal UserPromptSubmit, then PreToolUse admission, then tools/call: zero gates and a claude-entry ref bound to the plan digest) plus its no-entry negative. It also adds a Stop-pause denial test for retire/enroll/batch while the token is live, a token survive-then-spent-on-settle test, and a check that the lane gate still offers revision delegation. The tests match the runtime in lane_guard, mcp_server, kernel_ports and run_continuation, and the dist bundle mirrors the source.

advisory_findings.summary: Only the run_continuation PreToolUse hook enforces the Stop-boundary pause refusal. consumePhaseAdmission and requireRunEntry do not check the pause, and the new pause test asserts only the hook denial, not a tools/call refusal. The ADR describes this refusal as run_entry_required, but the hook's deny reason starts with 'Run paused:'.

evidence.trigger: Run paused at the Stop boundary with a live entry token, and the phase-entry PreToolUse hook has written an admission for retire_stale_batch → the tools/call side would still accept that admission if the continuation hook's deny were bypassed. Claude Code's PreToolUse deny blocks the call today, so there is no observable wrong result now; only defense in depth is missing.

findings.summary: A token-backed retire_stale_batch never records a confirmation_ref, so it records none of kind entry_token bound to the plan digest. The new claude-entry- reference kind is reachable only from a unit test.

evidence.trigger: A literal /imm-run mints a live token, then the model calls retire_stale_batch on a drifted batch. ClaudeRuntime.confirm returns {decision:'accept', requestId:'entry-token:<uuid>'}, and the gate returns {kind:'confirmed', request_id}. runtime/unattended/batch_disposition.ts retireStaleBatch, an unchanged file read because it is the state owner the changed caller kernel_ports.ts retireStaleBatch delegates to, discards request_id. It writes {...record, batch_state:'superseded'} and a report, and neither carries a confirmation_ref. The plan-digest-bound reference of kind entry_token that AC1 and Spec D2 require is never computed or persisted. confirmationRef() in interaction.ts, the only place the 'claude-entry-' kind is produced, has no caller on the retire path; git grep shows its only callers are kernel_ports.ts:448 (gate, which ENTRY_TOKEN_OPERATIONS never routes to with a token) and kernel_ports.ts:1097 (batch start, which keeps the native gate). The delivered test in tests/batch-stale-disposition.test.ts asserts only state==='retired' and gates===0. tests/claude-phase-entry-gate.test.ts checks the confirmationRef helper in isolation. No test shows that a retirement records the reference. Fix: bind and persist a confirmation_ref (kind entry_token, covering the plan digest) on the token-backed retirement, and add a test that reads it back from the retired record or report.

findings.summary: No delivered test covers the AC2 case 'a call after the run paused at the Stop boundary'. Nothing pins that retire_stale_batch, the one operation a live token now lets skip the native gate, is refused with no Kernel mutation once the run is paused.

evidence.trigger: Session with a live minted token → Stop hook pauses the run (decideRunContinuation returns pause, or stop_blocks reaches 7) → PreToolUse plus tools/call retire_stale_batch under the same token. Today the refusal rests only on retire_stale_batch being in NATIVE_OPERATIONS and on the missing correlation in requireRunEntry. No test exercises either step, so removing retire_stale_batch from NATIVE_OPERATIONS would let a paused run retire a batch with no gate and the suite would still pass. The only existing pause test (claude-run-continuation 'a failed native gate...') covers a PostToolUseFailure pause and enroll only.

findings.summary: The token-backed retire_stale_batch is never tested at the seam AC1 names: a literal UserPromptSubmit, then the PreToolUse admission, then tools/call. The only test injects ToolMeta.entryToken straight into ClaudeRuntime, and the RETIRE hook constant in claude-phase-entry-gate.test.ts is declared but never used.

evidence.trigger: UserPromptSubmit '/imm-run <slug>' → phaseEntryGateHookOutput writes a v2 admission for retire_stale_batch → handleJsonRpc tools/call retire_stale_batch. None of these new pieces is exercised end to end: the GATED_MCP_TOOL regex extension, the token carried in the admission, the workspace check in requireRunEntry, and passing entryToken into ToolMeta for retire. Also untested is the new refusal of retire_stale_batch with no prior entry, which tools/call accepted before this change. A regression that drops the token from the admission, or skips requireRunEntry for retire, would either reopen elicitation or retire with no entry, and the suite would still pass. batch-stale-disposition.test.ts only checks ClaudeRuntime.retireStaleBatch with a hand-supplied entryToken.

findings.summary: No test pins the AC3 token lifetime: still live after a same-session Stop continuation, spent once the bound run settles. The lane-mode dialog under a live token is opened in tests, but no test asserts that it still offers Lane revision delegation.

evidence.trigger: Live token → Stop hook returns block (continuation) → next retire_stale_batch must still be admitted. Bound run settles → runContinuationHookOutput calls revokeEntryToken(spent) → next retire_stale_batch must be refused. Neither transition is tested at the hook level: revokeEntryToken is never called in any test, and only the pure reducer line in phase-entry.test.ts is checked. A regression that revokes on every Stop, or never revokes on settle, would pass. The claude-batch-authority lane tests run under a minted token but assert only lane_mode.max_parallel and parallel_groups, never offer_revision_delegation.
